semantics.note: Keeps the antecedent ('even one') and the 'will' consequent. The proposition also folds in the present-tense premise that none can survive on their own, which is an observation and is not scored here. 'Without venture capital' fairly paraphrases 'VC is holding them up'.

contract.note: In context, reading 'current stack' as the heavily funded late-2025 AI companies is fair and ordinary. Reading 'dies' as shutting down or liquidation, not a restructuring, is reasonable. No horizon was stated, so the consequent can only be tested after a qualifying failure.

evidence.note: Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 on 2026-10-12 but kept operating, had stopped training models, and was much smaller than the leading labs. It is an ambiguous antecedent at best, and too recent to show any effect on fundraising or M&A.
OpenAI raised a record round in 2026, so the leading company did not falter. It shows no qualifying failure.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. No clear death of a major AI company from the late-2025 stack appears in the evidence. Character.AI's filing is ambiguous: it was still operating, a sale was pending, and it was a smaller firm. It also came too late to observe any effect on fundraising or M&A. The antecedent has not been shown to occur, so the consequent cannot be scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: He states an unhedged present state: these four firms make their money from other products, and 'AI is not doing it'. The proposition captures this.

contract.note: The plain reading, that AI was not a real source of their revenue or profit, is ordinary. Using the last quarter reported before the post is reasonable. 'Making money' could mean profit, which is not reported separately, but in everyday usage meaningful AI revenue counts. The contract flags this.

evidence.note: Alphabet's Q3 2025 earnings remarks name AI revenue as a key driver of Cloud growth. This is a company disclosure for the target quarter.
Alphabet says Q3 2025 revenue from products built on its generative AI models grew more than 200% year over year, and that its AI portfolio is lifting Cloud margins. This is a company disclosure.
Microsoft's $13B AI run rate is from January 2025, before the target quarter, and is annualized. Context only, though it points the same way.

reviews.rationale: The claim covers all four companies, and Alphabet's own Q3 2025 disclosures call AI revenue a key driver of Cloud growth, report generative AI product revenue up more than 200%, and say AI is improving Cloud margins. That meets the contradiction condition for at least one firm. The first half (they have other products making money) is uncontroversial. AI's net profit cannot be measured, and the figures are company-reported, not independent findings.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the 'does not appear' hedge. It leaves out the $412 share-price fact and the 'I imagine' guess about motives. The deal impression is the claim here.

contract.note: 'Does not appear to be happening' is an impression, and 'I imagine' marks speculation. Treating either as a firm claim that the deal was dead would overstate what he said, so not scoring it is fair.

reviews.rationale: The deal claim is a hedged impression ('does not appear'), and the cause of the stock move is openly a guess ('I imagine'). Under the policy, hedged language is not scored. The packet rightly contains no evidence.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Nobody appears to have worked out that' takes genAI being inherently unprofitable as given, so that premise is asserted, not hedged. The hedged, open-ended funding forecast is kept as a qualifier and not scored.

contract.note: 'Inherently unprofitable' and 'every single company' are categorical, so one credible counterexample is a fair test. One could argue 'every single company' means only VC-backed startups. But 'inherently' is about the technology itself, which supports the broader reading. The contract flags this.

evidence.note: In 2022 Midjourney's founder said the company was profitable and had no investors. This is self-reported and unaudited, but it is a direct counterexample within the period.
In August 2025 Midjourney was still investor-free and running independently, so it was not dependent on venture money. This does not prove profit by itself.

reviews.rationale: The firm premise is that genAI is inherently unprofitable, so every single company depends on venture money. Midjourney contradicts it: its founder reported it profitable and investor-free in 2022, and it was still investor-free in 2025. The evidence rests on founder statements, which the contract accepts, not audited figures. The forecast that funding must continue in perpetuity is hedged and not scored.
